units.la: ᴀᴅ ɪɔɔɔʟXVIII
DISPUTATIO THEOLOGICA DE Necessitate Satisfactionis Christi.
units.tr: Theological Disputation on the Necessity of Christ's Satisfaction.

units.la: THESIS I.
units.tr: THESIS I.

units.la: QUia Moses cum choro Prophetarum omnium scripserunt de Christo, idque factum ex inspiratione & directione Spiritus Dei ostendentis æternum Dei decretum, quomodo ex sapienti suo consilio homines per inobedientiam peccati regno mancipatos, & à Deo ejusque imagine alienatos, salvâ suâ perfectione, majestate, sanctitate & justitiâ, ad amicitiam, pacem perfectam, & possessionem cœlestis hæreditatis admittat, asseratque: id considerandum diligenter nobis venit.
units.tr: Since Moses, together with the whole choir of the prophets, wrote about Christ, and this was done by the inspiration and direction of the Spirit of God, who shows God's eternal decree, namely how God, by His wise counsel, admits to friendship, perfect peace and possession of the heavenly inheritance those who through disobedience have been enslaved to the kingdom of sin and alienated from God and His image, while His own perfection, majesty, holiness and justice remain intact, and affirms this, we must consider it carefully.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Nam constat, Christum Jesum propositum esse à Deo propitiationem per fidem in ipsius sanguine, hoc fine, ut demonstratio fieret ejus justitiæ, propter præteritionem & non punitionem antegressorum peccatorum. Quia scilicet, ut gloriam suam alteri Deus non dat; ita vindicat eam ab omni calumnia. Voluit itaque in exhibitione Messiæ declarare, se, qui justificat improbum per fidem, esse justum.
units.tr: For it is established that Jesus Christ was set forth by God as a propitiation through faith in his blood, for this end: that the demonstration of his justice might be made, on account of the passing over and non-punishment of former sins. For, as God does not give his glory to another, so he vindicates it from every calumny. He therefore willed, in the exhibition of the Messiah, to declare that he himself, who justifies the wicked through faith, is just.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Id fieri secus nequivit, nisi justitiæ ejus satisfieret. Quod, ut clariùs patescat, certo argumentorum ordine necessitatem satisfactionis pro expiatione peccatorum sum demonstraturus.
units.tr: This could not have come about otherwise unless his justice were satisfied. So that this may be made clearer, I shall demonstrate the necessity of satisfaction for the expiation of sins by a certain ordered series of arguments.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Eæ rationes sunt, quas natura ipsius Dei & revelatio suggerit.
units.tr: These are the reasons which the very nature of God and revelation suggest.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Deus enim est justus & sanctus, exaltatio ejus fit in judicio, ut & sanctificatio in justitia, Esa. 5:16. Necesse itaque est peccatum hominis judicari & puniri apud Deum, quia ille est constans, & gloriæ suæ vindex, & amans virtutum suarum. Iudicium requirit, ut factum malum, & legi sanctæ adversum laude & præmio non afficiatur, sed pœna & pudore, sive execratione. Et sanctitatis natura & proprietas est, cum peccato & malo commorari non posse. Psal. 5. Si namque aliter se habere res potest, potest factum turpe honestari; injustitia fieri justitia; profanitas sanctitas; infidelitas, fidelitas; tenebræ lux &c. & vice versa. Sed ut imago Diaboli non potest fieri imago Dei, sic, nisi justitiæ Dei satisfiat, nisi perfectiones ejus demonstrentur, peccatorem ad unionem sui admittere non potest.
units.tr: For God is just and holy; his exaltation is shown in judgment, and his sanctification in righteousness (Esa. 5:16). It is therefore necessary that man's sin be judged and punished before God, because he is constant, the avenger of his own glory, and a lover of his own virtues. Judgment requires that an evil deed, one opposed to the holy law, be not met with praise and reward but with punishment, shame, or execration. And it is the nature and property of holiness that it cannot dwell with sin and evil (Psal. 5). For if things could be otherwise, a shameful deed could be made honourable, injustice become justice, profanity holiness, unfaithfulness faithfulness, darkness light, and so on, and vice versa. But just as the image of the Devil cannot become the image of God, so, unless the justice of God is satisfied and his perfections are displayed, he cannot admit a sinner to union with himself.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Et hoc res ipsa clamat. Nam peccatum est contra Dei esse, & conatur, quantum in se est, destruere Deum. Non profecto, quasi id possit, sed quia homo ad imaginem Dei conditus, & dominio ejus subjectus, est obstrictus ad obsequium sancte erga Deum præstandum, legi naturæ primitus impressæ conformiter vivendum, exemplar suum exprimendum, unicum bonum, quod exsatiare potest, solum appetendum: si contraria faciat, negabit Deum esse Deum, justum judicem; negabit esse bonum, fruitionem mundi et præponendo; negabit omni obedientia & religione colendum; imo, dum cupiditatibus indulget, & Deum apprehendit justum judicem, & severum peccatorum vindicem, peccatis adversum & desideriis flagitiosis, non potest non exhorrescere, imo & odisse, quia scit, se reum condemnationis, & cuperet Deum ultorem impiorum non esse, vel saltem non esse talem, qualis est, sed, qui conniveret ad peccata, eaque ferret, & cum scelieratis, alienatis a vita Dei, simul curreret, cohabitaret, eos laude & præmio ornaret, & contemtores gloriæ divinæ frui tamen ea sineret. Unde liquet, quàm injuriosi & blasphemi sint adversus creatorem suum ii, qui, imaginem Dei contaminantes, ejus dominio & reverentia sese eximentes, & illi rebellantes, & ex luce tenebras efficere conantes, vel tollere Deum cupiunt, vel statuunt amantem peccati, eoque deliciari. Hoc enim sonat peccatori simile esse posse.
units.tr: And the thing itself cries out for this. For sin is against God's very being, and attempts, as far as it is in itself, to destroy God. Not indeed as though it could do so, but because man, made in the image of God and subject to his dominion, is bound to render holy obedience to God, to live in conformity with the law of nature first impressed upon him, to express his own pattern, and to seek the one good that can satisfy him alone. If he does the contrary, he will deny that God is God, the just judge; he will deny that the good is to be preferred to the enjoyment of the world; he will deny that God is to be worshipped with all obedience and religion. Indeed, while he indulges his lusts and yet apprehends God as the just judge and severe avenger of sins, he cannot but shudder, and even hate, because he knows himself to be liable to condemnation; and he would wish God not to be the avenger of the wicked, or at least not to be such as He is, but one who would connive at sins and tolerate them, run alongside the wicked, who are estranged from the life of God, live with them, adorn them with praise and reward, and still allow the contemners of divine glory to enjoy it. From this it is clear how injurious and blasphemous towards their Creator are those who, defiling the image of God, exempting themselves from his dominion and reverence, rebelling against him, and trying to make darkness out of light, either desire to remove God altogether or set up a God who loves sin and delights in it. For this is what it would amount to, to be like a sinner.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Et quid est Deum esse? Non equidem puto esse simpliciter majorem omnibus rebus, easque nosse & dirigere utcunque, & creaturis ratione investitis quadecunque causa & ratione & quomodo cunque habendum se præbere; sed esse summum, esse solum herum, beatum, sanctum & qui malum intueri non potest, & copiam fruitionis sui non dat nisi imperio ejus cum debita reverentia addictis. In hoc enim similes ipsi sunt, quia id judicant esse bonum, justum, honestum &c. quod & Deus, & id amant & approbant, quod & ipse, eoque oblectantur. Et his, nisi se abnegare velit, non potest non communicare. Contemtores vero sui, majestatis & celsitatis divinæ ingratos osores & vilipendentes non facere non experiri, qualem & quantum Dominum & bonum contemserint. Alioquin etenim suspectum se vel impotentiæ, quasi gloriam suam afferere nequeat; vel imperfectæ sanctitatis, ne dicam profanitatis, qui socius peccatorum & gloriæ ejus violatorum esse possit, reddet; quin & indigentiæ, quod non possit carere impuris illis hominibus. Quæ si sunt absurda, per satisfactionem justitiam Dei demonstrari oportet, quod fit in punitione peccati & obedientia legis.
units.tr: And what is it to be God? I do not think it is merely to be greater than all things, to know and direct them in some way, and to show oneself to rational creatures on whatever ground and in whatever manner. Rather it is to be supreme, the sole Lord, blessed, holy, and one who cannot look upon evil, and who gives the abundance of his enjoyment only to those devoted to his rule with due reverence. For in this they are like him: they judge that to be good, just and honourable which God also judges so, and they love and approve what he loves and approves, and take delight in it. And they cannot but share in these things, unless they wish to deny themselves. Those who despise his majesty and exalted glory, however, cannot fail to experience, as ungrateful haters and despisers, what kind and how great a Lord and good they have scorned. Otherwise he would render himself suspect, either of impotence, as if he could not assert his own glory, or of imperfect holiness, not to say profanity, as if he could be a companion of sinners and violators of his glory; nay, of neediness, in that he could not do without those impure men. If these things are absurd, the justice of God must be demonstrated through satisfaction, which takes place in the punishment of sin and in the obedience of the law.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Si, citra hoc, peccatori via pateret ad Deum & jus potiundi regno cœlorum, posset Deus non punire peccatum. Si hoc, non posset Deus punire peccatum. Id est, si enunciatum hoc esset verum, nempe: Deus potest non punire peccatum: hinc sequetur, Deum non posse punire peccatum. Quia non obest gloriæ & perfectioni divinæ, sive justitiæ & sanctitati & cæteris ejus virtutibus. Non enim est contra gloriam Dei, quia eam non lædit; siquidem citra abnegationem sui & virtutum suarum consortem naturæ suæ, participem vitæ, salutis, & beatitudinis æternæ hominem peccati sordibus inquinatum, nec lotum; Dei inimicum & hostem, nec reconciliatum; legi Dei subjici nescium, cujus sub perfectæ obedientiæ conditione compos constituitur bonorum Domini, facere poteset. Si, inquam, potest talem non punire, qui violat, & malitiose fertur ergá legem, quæ testatur Dei sanctitatem & justitiam, sive illa sit naturæ tantum indita, sive etiam revelata verbo, vel tradita & promulgata scripto, eo ipso testaretur Deus, legem istam non sancte & juste testari de natura, voluntate, & virtutibus divinis. Aliter enim se habere hæc possent, quàm testimonium legis dicit.
units.tr: If, apart from this, a way lay open for the sinner to God and a right to obtain the kingdom of heaven, God could refrain from punishing sin. If this were so, God could not punish sin. That is, if this proposition were true, namely, "God can refrain from punishing sin," it would follow that God cannot punish sin. For this would not harm the glory and perfection of God, that is, his justice, holiness and his other virtues. For it is not against the glory of God, since it does not injure it. For, without the denial of himself and of his virtues, God could make a man, defiled with the filth of sin and not washed, an enemy and foe of God and not reconciled, one who does not know how to submit to the law of God, a partaker of his nature, a sharer in life, salvation and eternal blessedness, and one who is made master of the good things of the Lord on condition of perfect obedience. I say, if he can fail to punish one who violates the law and is maliciously disposed toward it, the law which bears witness to the holiness and justice of God, whether that law is implanted in nature alone, or also revealed in the Word, or handed down and promulgated in writing, then by that very fact God would bear witness that this law does not truly and justly testify concerning the nature, will and virtues of God. For these things could be otherwise than the testimony of the law says.

units.la: Quia, quod lex perhibet Deum amare, idem Deus odisse posset, & amare, quod odisse. Et sic, quod est contra naturam, voluntatem & virtutes ejus, non effet contra illa. Et sic, si tamen puniret, testatum faceret, se non justa & æqua causa id facere, verùm, quia ita illi luberet, & quia delectaretur illis puniendis, & voluptatem caperet, opera manuum suarum, quæ ad gloriam suam formaverat, destruendo. Quod Deus non facit.
units.tr: Because whatever the law declares, that God loves, the same God could also hate, and love what he hates. And so what is contrary to his nature, will and virtues would not be contrary to them. And so, if he nevertheless punished, he would show that he does this not for a just and fair cause, but because it pleases him so, and because he takes delight in punishing and finds pleasure in destroying the works of his hands, which he had formed for his own glory. This God does not do.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Nam testatur de suis virtutibus, & in omnibus ejus operibus æquitas est. Justæ sunt ejus viæ, easque vult esse creaturæ rationalis semitas, sive lucernam & facem, quibus inspectis, officium hominis erga Dei voluntatem innotescat, & cognoscatur justitia, jus, & æquitas Dei, nec aliter ipsum se velle agere cum hominibus, quibus ea lex posita est, quàm ea, & totum Dei verbum docet. Ergo, si transgressores posset non punire, vel citra satisfactionem, injuriam Deo per transgressionem illatam, compensantem, unionem sui dare posset; injustum & iniquum esset eos punire. Quare? Quia ob id punirentur, quod non esset contra Dei perfectiones.
units.tr: For he bears witness to his own virtues, and in all his works there is equity. His ways are just, and he wills them to be the paths, or the lamp and torch, of the rational creature, so that, by looking at them, the duty of man toward the will of God may become known, and the justice, right and equity of God may be recognised; nor does he will to deal with men, to whom this law has been given, in any other way than this, as the whole Word of God teaches. Therefore, if he could fail to punish transgressors, or could give himself in union to them without satisfaction, making compensation for the injury done to God by the transgression, it would be unjust and iniquitous to punish them. Why? Because they would be punished for that which is not contrary to the perfections of God.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Sed & gentes agnoscunt, quòd, qui peccata faciunt, digni sint morte, sive indigni vita. Hoc autem tunc fit, quando Deus testatur de virtutibus suis, quas peccatores abnegant, & Deus non potest, cùm est necesse, de iis non testari, tanquam rebus ipsi charissimis, quò cognoscat creatura, Deum esse talem, qualis est.
units.tr: But the nations too acknowledge that those who commit sins are worthy of death, or unworthy of life. This, however, happens when God bears witness to his virtues, which sinners deny; and God cannot, when it is necessary, fail to bear witness to them, as to things most dear to himself, so that the creature may know God to be such as he is.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Sed cur longè abimus, cùm sacer codex non uno in loco doceat manifestè, Deum esse ignem consumentem, Exod. 24: 17. 13: 7. qui nullo pacto absolvit scilicet fontem, visitat peccata patrum in filios, in filios filiorum, in nepotes, & abnepotes. Quæ certè indicant, Deum non posse dimittere peccatum inultum, neque aliter salutem hominibus posse dare, nisi peccatum deleatur, nisi legi satisfiat, & nisi ejus perfectio omnis cum gloria demonstretur.
units.tr: But why do we go far afield, when the sacred writings teach plainly in more than one place that God is a consuming fire (Exod. 24: 17; 13: 7), who by no means acquits the guilty, and visits the sins of the fathers upon the children, the children's children, the grandchildren and great-grandchildren? These things certainly indicate that God cannot let sin go unpunished, nor can he otherwise give salvation to men, unless sin is blotted out, unless the law is satisfied, and unless all his perfection is displayed together with his glory.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Gloria ejus demonstratur in eo, quòd proposuit suum testamentum, in quo continetur ejus consilium, quo destinavit hæredes fieri eos justitiæ æternæ per Christum excisum adducendæ, qui per gratiam ipsius arcem Dei apprehensuri erant, & sunt, & pacem cum Deo facerent. Dixit enim post lapsum, inimicitiam se positurum inter Diabolum & mulierem, & inter semen utriusque, semen vero mulieris contriturum caput serpentis; serpentem autem tem calcem feminis mulieris contriturum, & morsuum. Ubi in-nuitur sanctificatio feminis mulieris. Aliter enim illa inimicitia poni non potest, nisi posito odio inter semen utrumque. At hoc fieri, nisi justificetur semen mulieris, nequaquam potest. Et ad hoc requiritur condemnatio peccati, & interemtio legis; unde vim condemnandi hominem jus in eum petendo ad imperio mortis subjiciendum, peccatum accipiebat. Et Abrahamo Deus promissionem fecit, quod in semine ipsius benedicentur gentes, sed ejus rationem & modum non explicuit prius, quam quum Mosi apparens proclamavit, se quidem esse misericordem, gratiosum, longanimem, multum benignitate & fide, qui custodit benignitatem millibus, & condonantem iniquitatem & defectionem & peccatum: sed, qui absolvendo non absolvit, vel non habet impunitum, verum visitat iniquitatem patrum in filios, & in filios filiorum, nepotes & abnepotes. Hic jam elucet ratio condonationis, benedictionis, positionis inimicitiae, & contritionis capitis serpentis. Et sane, si justum est apud Deum, reddere afflictionem iis, qui affligunt fideles; justum est etiam bona in virtutibus statim enumeratis nota seminis sanctificato sic dare, & non aliter, ut justitia Dei maneat integra. Id autem fit per satisfactionem, sive impletionem legis, & precium sufficiens redimendis in potestatem Satanae, pernicioso ejus consilio recepto, redactis. de quo in sequentibus.
units.tr: His glory is displayed in this, that he set forth his covenant, in which is contained his counsel, by which he purposed that those who were to be brought to eternal justice, cut off through Christ, should become heirs, who by his grace were to lay hold of the stronghold of God, and have peace with God, and do so. For after the fall he said that he would put enmity between the Devil and the woman, and between the seed of each, and that the seed of the woman would bruise the head of the serpent, while the serpent would bruise the heel of the woman's seed, and bite it. Here the sanctification of the woman's seed is implied. For that enmity cannot be set up otherwise, unless hatred is set between the two seeds. But this cannot happen unless the seed of the woman is justified. And for this the condemnation of sin and the abolition of the law are required; whence sin received the power to condemn a man, by claiming a right against him to subject him to the dominion of death. And to Abraham God made the promise that in his seed all the nations would be blessed, but he did not explain its reason and manner before, when appearing to Moses, he proclaimed that he is indeed merciful, gracious, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and faithfulness, who keeps mercy for thousands, and forgives iniquity and transgression and sin; but who, in forgiving, does not acquit, nor leaves the guilty unpunished, but visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Here now the reason of forgiveness, of blessing, of the setting of enmity, and of the bruising of the serpent's head becomes clear. And indeed, if it is just with God to render affliction to those who afflict the faithful, it is also just to give the good things, noted in the virtues just enumerated, to the sanctified seed in this way and in no other, so that the justice of God may remain entire. This, however, is done through satisfaction, that is, the fulfilment of the law, and a price sufficient to redeem those who had been brought under the power of Satan, which they had accepted through his pernicious counsel. Of this more in what follows.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Amplius patet ex dialogismo inter Deum Patrem & Filium ejus instituto; Ubi Pater agit, ut judex justus, justitiae suae assertor constantissimus (quod etiam titulus in vindicatione gloriae appositus [Hebrew], zelus, ut & cum dicitur [Hebrew] praeditus excandescentia Nah. 1:2. ostendit) non alia ratione homines jam lapsos amicitiam ejus inire posse, quam data satisfactione. Hoc postulatum Patris Esa. 53:10. Si posuerit anima ipsius (Christi) ascham, videbit semen, prolongabit dies & beneplacitum Jehova per eum prosperabitur. ubi conditio ponitur Christo, promisso femine proventuro, si ipse ponat [Hebrew] quod non significat hoc loco reatum vel culpam, sed id, quod requiritur ad reatum solvendum. Ille enim, a quo hoc exigitur, est expers omnis vitii, nec mors ejus dicenda reatus vel culpa; sed invitatur ad hoc, ut solvat reatum eorum, quorum promissio, & dierum prolongatio hic proponitur in operae precium pro labore praestituto. Non enim vocatur ut, frustra la-boboret, & inaniter, vanéque vires suas consumat, sed sub conditione mer-cedis reddendæ. Christus propositam conditionem cum præmio ei annexo amplectitur cum gaudio Hebr. 12:2. & spondet, quo gloriosus in oculis Dei est, & quo voluptas ejus proficiat: Adsum, ut voluntatem tuam faciam. Voluntas Dei est quærere semen. semen non quæritur sine sanctificatione; sanctificatio non sine justificatione antecedente; nec justificatio improbi Sforzo esse potest, nisi demonstretur ejus justitia. Hoc Deus quærebat, ad hoc efficiendum Christus seipsum, ut promptum & voluntarium servum offert. Ira enim Dei, quæ ardet adversus iniquitatem, hoc, & non alio remedio avertitur.
units.tr: It appears further from the dialogue instituted between God the Father and his Son. There the Father acts as a just judge, the most constant asserter of his own justice (as the title applied in the vindication of his glory, [Hebrew], zeal, and the phrase [Hebrew], endowed with wrath, Nah. 1:2, show). He declares that men already fallen can enter into his friendship by no other way than by a given satisfaction. This is the Father's demand in Isa. 53:10: If his soul shall make itself an offering for sin [Hebrew: asham], he shall see seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper through him. Here a condition is laid upon Christ, with the promise of seed to come if he himself should set down [Hebrew], which in this place does not mean guilt or fault, but what is required to discharge guilt. For he from whom this is demanded is free from every vice, and his death is not to be called guilt or fault. Rather he is invited to this, that he should discharge the guilt of those whose offspring and prolonged days are here set before him as a reward worth the labour he undertakes. He is not called to labour in vain, to spend his strength to no purpose and emptily, but under the condition of a reward to be paid. Christ embraces the proposed condition, with the reward annexed to it, with joy (Heb. 12:2), and promises, by which he becomes more glorious in the eyes of God and by which his pleasure advances: Lo, I come to do your will. The will of God is to seek seed. Seed is not sought without sanctification; sanctification is not possible without a prior justification; and the justification of the wicked cannot be Sforzo unless his justice is demonstrated. This God was seeking, and to accomplish this Christ offers himself as a ready and willing servant. For the wrath of God, which burns against iniquity, is averted by this remedy and by no other.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Et, quia gentes Christo dantur in hæreditatem, & fines terræ in possessionem, ut non lux tantum, sed salus quoque eis obtingat, constat eas ante sine Deo fuisse, & quidem ob justum Dei judicium, iramque. Quæ ira obstabat gratiæ & paci Dei his donandæ, antequam possent esse hæreditas Christi & peculium acquisitum. Ira enim Dei eos disperserat, ut irent in viis suis. Et, quia Christo Regi inuncto reddmuntur, id manifesto argumento est, non prius quivisse illos ad politiam cœlestem pertinere, quam ira Dei justa illis incumbens tolleretur, pace illis impetrata. Hoc factum, Lytro soluto, ideo, ut Deus, qui fuit læsus, demonstraretur justus, & vindex gloriæ suæ, & liqueret, satisfactione perfecta opus esse hæreditaturis regnum cœleste, nec eo sufficere acceptilationem qualiscunque justitiæ, sed quæ testimonium det justitiæ Dei integerrimæ, & ab omni impuritate separatæ, eumque gloriosum & admirabilem in omnibus operibus suis ostendat. Excellenter autem gloriosus ut & admirabilis fit, dum voluntas illius præstatur ad demonstrationem justitiæ suæ, quæ nullam eclipsin & nullam claudicationem patitur, exactione, & exhibitione talis & tantæ satisfactionis, qualis & quanta sufficiat iræ Dei relaxandæ, imo remittendæ, sine diminutione divini honoris. Alias æquitas non fuisset in rejectione gentium, cæteris in peculium interim assumtis.
units.tr: And because the Gentiles are given to Christ as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth as a possession, so that not only light but also salvation should fall to them, it is plain that they were formerly without God, and indeed on account of God's just judgment and wrath. That wrath stood in the way of the grace and peace of God to be bestowed on them, before they could become the inheritance of Christ and a peculiar people. For the wrath of God had scattered them, so that they walked in their own ways. And because they are given back to Christ the anointed King, this is a clear argument that they could not belong to the heavenly commonwealth before the just wrath of God resting upon them was removed and peace was obtained for them. This was done, with the ransom paid, so that God, who had been wronged, might be shown to be just and the avenger of his own glory, and so that it might be made clear that the heavenly kingdom must be inherited through a perfected satisfaction, and that an acceptance of some kind of righteousness is not enough, but one which bears witness to the most perfect righteousness of God, separated from all impurity, and which shows him to be glorious and admirable in all his works. Moreover he is shown to be most excellently glorious and admirable, while his will is carried out to demonstrate his righteousness, which suffers no eclipse and no limping, by the exacting and the rendering of such and so great a satisfaction as is sufficient to relax, or rather to remit, the wrath of God, without any diminution of the divine honour. Otherwise there would have been no fairness in the rejection of the Gentiles while the others were meanwhile taken into the peculiar people.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: Adde his, quòd omnes peccarunt, & non est justus, ne unus quidem, non est, qui intelligat, non est, qui quærat bonum. Omnes deflexerunt, simul inutiles facti sunt, non est, qui faciat benignitatem &c. Rom.3:10–18. Rom. 11.32. Gal.3.22. Unde, si omnes sunt ita sub peccato & inobedientia, ut non possint bonum facere; sunt etiam injusti & venditi sub peccato & imperio vel dominio peccati, & sub mortis regno sunt, ut exurgendi ab eo potestatem non habeant. Et tamen Deus non incassum omnes homines creavit, sed ut habitent decu Dei etiam refractarii. Ex sese homines vires exeundi ex ea miseria, in quam pariter omnes inciderunt, non habent. Necesse itaque est redimi illos. Quod fit per pietii sufficientis & idonei, ad illos emendum & asserendum in libertatem, solutionem. Quod ipsum Dei propositum ostendit, qui vult illorum misereri.
units.tr: Add to these that all have sinned, and there is not a righteous man, not even one; there is none who understands, there is none who seeks after good. All have turned aside; together they have become unprofitable; there is none who does kindness, etc. (Rom. 3:10–18; Rom. 11:32; Gal. 3:22). Hence, if all are so under sin and disobedience that they cannot do good, they are also unrighteous and sold under sin, under the power or dominion of sin, and under the kingdom of death, so that they have no power to rise out of it. Yet God did not create all men in vain, but that the Lord God might dwell even among the rebellious. Men do not have of themselves the strength to escape that misery into which they have all alike fallen. It is therefore necessary that they be redeemed. This is done through a sufficient and fitting price, a ransom to buy them back and to assert them into liberty. This very purpose of God shows it, since he wills to have mercy on them.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Ac, quoniam Deus non est prodigus virtutum suarum, nec immemor comminationis intimatur homini, si transgrediatur præceptum, miseratio illa non tollit, sed stabilit veritatem Dei, & exitus è morte sic patere misero peccatori potest, si in redemtione hominis cognoscitur Deus justus, sanctus, & misericors eo modo, quo rite & sanctè ab homine peccatore amari, & glorificari ob benignitatem suam queat, & ob quod ipsi etiam angeli cum admiratione eum celebrent. Ea autem ratio non alia est, quàm illa Dei sapientia, qua remedium invenit miserendi eorum, qui ob inobedientiam obnoxii erant severo Dei judicio, filii mortis, & damnationis æternæ rei. Et hæc est sapientia, hoc arcanum illud religiosè mirandum, quòd unà cum misericordia Dei illa etiam justitia resplendet, quæ docet, tam necessariam esse punitionem peccati, ut, absque hoc, si fiat remissio & condonatio, Deus se ipsum abneget, & sit aliud, quam Jehova significat.
units.tr: And since God is not prodigal of his virtues, and is not forgetful of the threat he has announced to man if he transgresses the precept, that mercy does not abolish but establishes the truth of God; and a way out of death can thus lie open to the wretched sinner, if in the redemption of man God is recognised as just, holy and merciful, in such a manner that he may be duly and holily loved and glorified by a sinner for his goodness, and on account of which the angels themselves also celebrate him with admiration. Now this plan is nothing other than that wisdom of God by which he found a remedy for having mercy on those who, through disobedience, were liable to the severe judgment of God, sons of death and bound to eternal damnation. And this is the wisdom, this the mystery to be religiously wondered at: that together with the mercy of God there also shines forth that justice which teaches that the punishment of sin is so necessary that, without it, if remission and pardon were granted, God would deny himself and would be other than what the name Jehovah signifies.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: Hoc porrò inde manifestum fit, quòd non alia lex hominem justificat, quam quæ & damnat. Et per eam sententiam, quæ æternam & immutabilem Dei veritatem promulgat: Homo, qui fecerit ea, vivet in illis: &, Maledictus omnis, qui non manserit in omnibus scriptis in libro legis, ut ea faciat. Vel ergo secundùm hanc legem procedit jujudicium Dei, vel alius est Deus, alia veritas, fidelitas, & voluntas ejus, quam hæ sententiæ enunciant. Hoc vero dicere de Deo non abest à blasphemia, & calumnia sanctissimæ ejus naturæ. Prius igitur verum manet, quod omnem laudem Deo ascribit.
units.tr: Moreover, it follows from this that no law justifies a man except the one that also condemns him. For by that sentence, which proclaims the eternal and unchangeable truth of God: "The man who does those things shall live in them," and "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the law, to do them" (Gal. 3:10; Lev. 18:5). Either, then, the judgment of God proceeds according to this law, or God is another being, and his truth, faithfulness and will are other than these sentences declare. Yet to say this of God is not far from blasphemy and slander against his most holy nature. The former therefore stands true, which ascribes all praise to God.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: Hujus veritas astruitur utique etiam exinde, quòd ex ea execratione Christus nos exemit, in quam propter transgressionem incideramus; quæ execratio fuit fructus inobedientiæ nostræ. Et ideo factus est sub legem ut nos ab ea redimeret: quæ fuit lex operum, eaque nobis jus petendæ hæreditatis ex perfectè præstita obedientia dabat, ut supra dictum. Cui quoniam contrarium fecimus, gratia, amicitia, amore & omnibono Dei excidimus, & vitam æternam in fœdere nobis promissam amisimus, & in mortem æternam, omnemque execrationem incidimus. Necessario itaque, dum Christus pro nobis factus est sub eam legem, diciturque factus execratio, portavit execrationem nobis debitam; lic et sanctus & immunis ab omni labe peccati. Et hæc est ratio, cur agnus tollens peccatum mundi Joh. 1: 29. item serpens exaltatus Joh. 3: 14. dicatur. Quia in ipsum sponsorem nostrum & sacerdotem iniquitatem nostram expiantem factum peccata nostra incurrere Deus fecerat Esa. 53:6. Nam homo peccator asserere se & alios in libertatem non potuit, ut, cui legis impletio, ob carnis infirmitatem, erat impossibilis. Hinc oportuit Christum intervenire, in cujus carne lex damnaretur & fieret lex spiritus vitæ in Christo. Quod & omnia sacrificia & typi ostendunt, nosque dirigunt ac ducunt ad satisfactionem in Christo inveniendam. In illis enim non poterat conscientia cultorum consummari, nec peccata per ea auferri.
units.tr: The truth of this is also established from the fact that Christ freed us from that curse into which we had fallen because of transgression, a curse which was the fruit of our disobedience. And for this reason he was made under the law, that he might redeem us from it. That law was the law of works, which gave us, on the basis of perfect obedience rendered, a right to claim the inheritance, as was said above. Since we did the opposite of this, we fell from grace, friendship, love and every good thing of God, we lost the eternal life promised to us in the covenant, and we fell into eternal death and every curse. Necessarily, therefore, while Christ was made under that law on our behalf, and is said to have been made a curse, he bore the curse due to us, while himself holy and free from every stain of sin. And this is the reason why he is called "the lamb that takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29), and likewise "the serpent lifted up" (John 3:14). For God had made our sins fall upon him, our surety and priest who was making atonement for our iniquity (Isa. 53:6). For a sinful man could not set himself or others free, since for him, on account of the weakness of the flesh, fulfilling the law was impossible. Hence it was necessary for Christ to intervene, in whose flesh the law would be condemned and would become "the law of the Spirit of life in Christ." All the sacrifices and types also show this, and direct and lead us to find satisfaction in Christ. For in those sacrifices the conscience of the worshippers could not be made complete, nor could sins be taken away through them.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Et, quia per Christum salus & remissio peccatorum annunciatur, Act. 13: 38. & justificatio ab omnibus illis, quibus in lege Mosis justificari non poterant, credenti in Christum certò datur, v. 39. clarum est, unicum remedium liberationis ab execratione omni esse satisfactionem Christi; in quo solo, & nullo alio in cœlo vel terra, vita & salus reperitur Act. 4. 12.
units.tr: And since salvation and the remission of sins are announced through Christ, Acts 13:38, and justification from all those things from which they could not be justified under the law of Moses is certainly given to one who believes in Christ, v. 39, it is clear that the only remedy for deliverance from all curse is the satisfaction of Christ; in him alone, and in no other under heaven or on earth, is life and salvation found, Acts 4:12.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: Et, quia ab initio multi introducti fuerant in cœlum, sive gloriam Dei, etiam ante adventum & incarnationem Christi, Hebr. 2:10. 12:23. hoc fieri non potuit, nisi ex fœdere gratiæ, & electione facta in ipso Christo ante fundationem mundi Eph.1.& ejus sponsione, qui illos asseruit & bajulavit Ef.63.9.nam ex operibus legis omnis caro coram Deo non justificatur Rom. 3. 20. oportuit principem salutis eorum, fratrem primogenitum, Goël & primitias per passiones consummari, ut Deus justus, justificans improbum ex fide, justificaretur, nec coelum, & in eo Deus, ob non punita peccata inquinaretur.
units.tr: And because many were brought into heaven, that is, into the glory of God, from the beginning, even before the coming and incarnation of Christ, Heb. 2:10; 12:23, this could not have happened except by the covenant of grace, by the election made in Christ himself before the foundation of the world, Eph. 1, and by his promise, who vouched for them and bore them up, Isa. 63:9. For no flesh is justified before God by the works of the law, Rom. 3:20. It was necessary that the prince of their salvation, their elder brother, the Goël and the firstfruits, be made perfect through sufferings, so that God, being just, might be shown to be just in justifying the wicked by faith, and so that heaven, and God who dwells in it, might not be defiled by sins left unpunished.

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Scopus Dei creantis hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem suam (qui & se & posteros praecipitavit in ruinam, cuique impossibile erat vel resurgere ex lapsu vel reconciliari ex sese Deo) certè non fuit blasphemari, nec ullam ab eo laudem capere: sed amari, glorificari, celebrari. Hoc fieri non potuit, nisi esset peccatori amabilis. Id effici non potuit concedendo ipsi usum coeli, solis, lunae, siderum, terrae, maris; cumulando etiam multis beneficiis; invitando ad obedientiam promisso praemio; & lege etiam data: quandiu vindex peccatorum apprehenditur. Quia etiam post peccatum obligatur homo & ad obedientiam erga Deum dominum suum, & ad poenam ob peccatum, in quo est terror ex metu judicii ortus. unde ad fugam & odium Dei incitatur. Hoc Deus non ignoravit, etiam ante creationem. Habuit ergo decretum efficiendi magnalia illa erga hominem, per quae digne & sancte ab eo & agnosceretur, & amaretur cum glorificatione, ob sufficientiam salvandi, sapientiam, qua viam miserandi homines sine abnegatione sui invenit, & ex bonitate sua exsequutus est. Quod aeque factu est impossibile, divinaeque veritati repugnans, non suppositá satisfactione, ac Deum non esse Deum.
units.tr: God's purpose in creating man in his own image and likeness (man who plunged himself and his posterity into ruin, and for whom it was impossible either to rise again from the fall or to be reconciled to God by his own powers) was certainly not that God should be blasphemed or receive any praise from him, but that he should be loved, glorified and celebrated. This could not happen unless God were lovable to a sinner. It could not be brought about by granting him the use of heaven, sun, moon, stars, earth and sea; by heaping many benefits upon him; by inviting him to obedience with a promised reward; or even by giving the law, so long as God is apprehended as the avenger of sins. For after sin man is bound both to obedience towards God his Lord and to punishment for sin, and in this there arises a terror from the fear of judgment, whence he is driven to flee from God and to hate him. God did not fail to foresee this, even before creation. He therefore had a decree to accomplish those great works toward man through which he would be worthily and holily acknowledged and loved by him, with glorification, on account of his sufficiency to save and his wisdom, by which he found a way of showing mercy to men without self-denial, and which he carried out from his goodness. This is equally impossible, and repugnant to divine truth, without a satisfaction being presupposed, as for God not to be God.

units.la: XXII.
units.tr: XXII.

units.la: Veteres expectarunt salutem Dei, & de ea sunt gloriati, ut Jacob Gen.49:18. Id sine dubio confirmat veritatem assertionis nostrae. Ea enim robur suum fundat in ea dilectione, redemtione, justificatione & adoptione, qua nos a Deo diligimur, & cui innituntur [Hebrew]. Illi in intimis non aliud revelatum fuit, quam verum [Hebrew] & expiatio vera, ejusque fundamentum. Hujus enim efficaciam, vel preciositatem, non sibi, vel domui suae ejusque rectitudini, sed foederi perpetuo, quod est Dei testamentum, cujus genimen est salus, asscribebat. Vide 2. Sam.23:5. Non est recta domus mea cum Deo, sed foedus perpetuum posuit mihi, dispositum inter omnes & servatum, quod omnis salus mea & omne beneplacitum erit. Quod aliud ab eo non est, quàm quod Abraham videre gestivit, & videndo gavi-sus est, Joh. 8. 56. & ex quo justificationem adeptus est. Rom. 4. Id autem est δικαίωμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων. Ergo satisfactio, extra quam non putarunt ullam salutem, ullum solidum gaudium, posse dari.
units.tr: The ancients looked for the salvation of God and boasted of it, as Jacob does in Genesis 49:18. This doubtless confirms the truth of our assertion. For their confidence rested on that love, redemption, justification and adoption by which we are loved by God and on which they depend [Hebrew]. To them nothing was revealed in its inner meaning except the true [Hebrew] and the true expiation, and its foundation. They ascribed its efficacy and preciousness not to themselves, or to their house, or to its uprightness, but to the everlasting covenant, which is the testament of God, whose offspring is salvation. See 2 Samuel 23:5: My house is not so with God, but he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure; for this is all my salvation and all my desire. This is nothing other than what Abraham longed to see, and seeing it rejoiced (John 8:56), and by which he obtained justification (Romans 4). This is the [δικαίωμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων] justification from many trespasses. Therefore satisfaction, outside which they thought no salvation and no solid joy could be given, is the point.

units.la: XXIII.
units.tr: XXIII.

units.la: Sed & natura fidei, ex qua vivitur, Habac. 2:4. Hebr. 10:38. huic succinit. Ea enim credit: qui fecerit, vivet in praeceptis, & non faciens sit maledictus. Et hinc ratiocinatur, Deum semper sui similem manere, cujus verba haec sunt. Et tamen, quanquam sciat neminem hominum legem servare, fidelitati & promissionibus divinis adhaerens, nec ad alium clivum se subducens, vitam & salutem apud Deum quaerit & ab eo exspectat. Et id quidem, cum divina decentia, salvo ejus jure, sanctitate, & justitia, & veracitate immutabili. Colligit itaque, firmiterque concludit, satisfactionis necessitatem. Sine tali fide ad Deum non acceditur cum filiali fiducia, quod satis vel ex Daniele liquet, cap. 9.
units.tr: The nature of faith, by which one lives (Habakkuk 2:4; Hebrews 10:38), agrees with this. For faith believes: "he who does these things shall live in them, and he who does not do them shall be cursed." And from this it reasons that God always remains like himself, whose words these are. Yet, although it knows that no man keeps the law, faith clings to the divine faithfulness and promises, does not withdraw itself to any other slope, and seeks and expects life and salvation from God. And this indeed is done consistently with the divine fitness, with his right, holiness, justice and unchanging truthfulness. Therefore it gathers, and firmly concludes, the necessity of satisfaction. Without such faith one does not draw near to God with filial trust, which is clear enough even from Daniel 9.

units.la: XXIV.
units.tr: XXIV.

units.la: Id, quod fide apprehensum per spem expectarunt a Deo, vi testamentariae dispositionis nitebatur. Confirmatio ejus sine sanguine & morte testatoris rata non est. Heb 9:16.17. Unde prius quoque Testam. V. scilicet, initiari sine sanguine non potuit, v. 18. quod figurabat mortem Filii Dei futuram per fusum sanguinem, ut jure communionis ex filiatione haereditatem acciperemus. Quod nos docet & esus sacrificiorum sive victimarum, & communio altaris, communio etiam sacerdotis, in iis, quorum partem illi sacerdotes comedebant, pro peccato; partem etiam sacrificantes per eos expiati: ut inde certi essent & veri altaris divinae Christi naturae, & naturae humanae in veram victimam peccata expiantem offerendae, se participes esse, & hoc ipso coram Deo consistere, nec sine hoc posse. Quod negare, est vel caeci, vel temerarii, vel hostis Dei & θεομάχος. Haec enim clamant, pacem, salutem & vitam conferri peccatoribus non posse, nec Deum decere dare, non intercedente sacrificio idoneo. Cui attestatur ipsa hominis conscientia, summa & a se inextricabilis malitiae devicti. vide saltem Esa. 6. 59. & medelam circa finem capitis ejusdem per Goel ex foedere Dei gratuito constitutum. ut & Esa. 63. & 53. &c.
units.tr: What they grasped by faith and awaited from God through hope rested on the force of a testamentary disposition. Its confirmation is not valid without the blood and death of the testator (Hebrews 9:16–17). Hence also the former testament could not be initiated without blood (v. 18), which prefigured the future death of the Son of God through shed blood, so that by the right of communion we might receive the inheritance through sonship. The eating of the sacrifices or victims teaches us this, and also the communion of the altar and the communion of the priest, in those things of which the priests ate a part, for sin, and the sacrificers too were atoned for by them in part. Thus they might be certain that they were partakers of the true altar, of the divine nature of Christ and of the human nature to be offered as the true victim expiating sins, and by this very fact stand before God, and could not do so without it. To deny this is the mark of the blind, the rash, or an enemy of God and a [θεομάχος] fighter against God. For these things cry out that peace, salvation and life cannot be bestowed on sinners, nor is it fitting for God to give them, unless a fitting sacrifice intervenes. To this the conscience of man itself bears witness, overcome by the greatest malice which it cannot disentangle from itself. See at least Isaiah 6 and 59, and the remedy toward the end of the same chapter, through the Redeemer (Goel) established by the free covenant of God, and also Isaiah 63 and 53, etc.

units.la: Absque hoc homo salutis cupidus & cum conscientia peccati collusatus vel constituitur in statu desperato, vel est idololatra, & superstitionis nefariæ plenus: ut alia omittam. Nam in tota vita omnibus tentationibus obvia & circumdata, & in morte exitum felicem vel miserum habitura, solidam, firmam, & immobilem consolationem, nisi, supposito plenissimo Christi sacrificio omnia peccata sufficientissimè auferente, & gratia Dei in hoc relucente, & lapsus frequentes, quotidianosque errores condonante, & ad finem usque potenter conservante, fiducia sui & propriæ justitiæ turgidus (etiam mistæ secundum tales) habere non potest. Impotens enim caro est. Vel, si temerè mente carnis inflatus persistat in opinione erronea, se, vires suas, & creaturam Deum suum statuet. Hoc ita se habet, quia negat meritum Christi, suarum virium putat potentiam credendi sine Spiritu Dei legem Dei nobis inscribente ad veram fidem & resipiscentiam, negatque, sola gratia Dei regenerationem, justificationem & spem vivam in peccatoribus produci. Et quæ non alia infinita gloriæ Dei, sanctitati ejus, legi & juri, atque gratiæ repugnantia hinc nascuntur? At doctrina sana gloriam Dei illustrat, studium pietatis excitat, auxilium Dei implorat, consolationem immotam in omnibus tentationibus, etiam morte, de charitate Dei in Christo perpetua porrigit.
units.tr: Apart from this, a man desirous of salvation, who has trifled with a consciousness of sin, either is placed in a state of despair, or becomes an idolater, full of wicked superstition, to pass over other things. For in the whole of life, exposed and surrounded by all temptations, and about to have a happy or wretched end in death, he cannot have solid, firm and immovable consolation, unless, on the supposition of the most complete sacrifice of Christ, which entirely removes all sins, and the grace of God shining forth in this, forgiving frequent lapses and daily errors and powerfully preserving to the end, he be puffed up with confidence in himself and in his own righteousness (even if mixed, according to such men). For the flesh is powerless. Or, if, inflated rashly by the mind of the flesh, he persists in an erroneous opinion, he will set up himself, his own strength, and the creature as his god. This is so because he denies the merit of Christ, thinks the power of believing is in his own strength without the Spirit of God writing the law of God in us for true faith and repentance, and denies that regeneration, justification and living hope are produced in sinners by the grace of God alone. And what other infinite things, opposed to the glory of God, to his holiness, law and right, and to grace, arise from this? But sound doctrine illustrates the glory of God, stirs up zeal for godliness, implores the help of God, and offers an unshaken consolation in all temptations, even in death, from the perpetual love of God in Christ.

units.la: XXVI.
units.tr: XXVI.

units.la: Christus enim satisfactione sua jus petendi & exspectandi vitam æternam nobis peperit, suaa cum omnibus ad vitam & pietatem pertinentibus. Is enim veniens à Patre missus in similitudine carnis peccati, & pro peccato, condemnavit peccatum in carne, ut jus legis impleretur in nobis non ambulantibus secundum carnem. Rom.8:3.4. Damnatum est peccatum, mortua lex. Demonstrata justitia Dei, sanctitas & misericordia, in mediatore. Unde Deus justus & sanctus justificatus & sanctificatus est. Hoc precium sufficiens gratiæ Dei impetrandæ & in nos à Christo redundaturæ.
units.tr: For by his satisfaction Christ obtained for us the right to seek and expect eternal life, together with all things that pertain to life and godliness. For he, sent by the Father and coming in the likeness of sinful flesh, and as an offering for sin, condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh. Rom. 8:3.4. Sin has been condemned, the law is dead. The justice of God, his holiness and mercy, has been displayed in the mediator. Whence God, being just and holy, is justified and sanctified. This is a price sufficient to obtain the grace of God, and it is to flow over into us from Christ.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Nam Christus est sponsor loco & vice nostri reorum, & sacerdos in iis, quæ ad Deum, & quæ ad gloriam Dei demonstrandam sunt, constitutus. Hebr.7:22–26.27.3:1.4:15. Si sponsor; debita nostra in se recepit, causam nostram suam fecit, in locum nostri substitutus. stitit. Quà sacerdos, victima se pro nobis obtulit, peccata in se conjecta portavit, expiavit & abstulit, gratiam Dei nobis conciliavit, &, ut Dominus gloriæ, ex regno peccati, tenebrarum & mortis, transtulit in regnum gratiæ, lucis & vitæ. Quod cùm perfectissimè nobis sit impetratum per Filium Dei spiritu æterno se offerentem Patri, firma & spes & gloriatio nostra, firma salutis acquisitio.
units.tr: For Christ is appointed surety in the place and stead of us who are guilty, and priest in those things which pertain to God and to the demonstration of God's glory. Heb. 7:22–26, 27; 3:1; 4:15. As surety, he took our debts upon himself, made our cause his own, and stood in our place. As priest, he offered himself as a victim for us, bore the sins laid upon him, expiated and took them away, reconciled us to God, and, as Lord of glory, transferred us from the kingdom of sin, darkness and death into the kingdom of grace, light and life. Since this has been obtained for us most perfectly through the Son of God, who offered himself to the Father by the eternal Spirit, it is our firm hope and boast, and the firm acquisition of salvation.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Certitudo & efficacia hujus tanta & tam indubitata in nos fluens constat ex relatione Christi sponsoris, & sacerdotis, regisque nostri in nos arctissima, & nostri ad eum: quia ille est caput nostrum, nos ipsius membra, ille princeps salutis nostræ, frater primogenitus, ille vitis, nos palmites, particeps carnis & sanguinis nostri, eo fine, ut imperium mortis habentem aboleret, & à metu mortis nos liberaret. Unde, quicquid, quà talis, Christus fecit, passus est, acquisivit, & habet; nostra, qui sumus illius membra, populus & peculium, censentur, & rata à Patre ipsi in hæreditatem datis inalienabiliter habentur & confirmantur. pro quibus omnibus, & solis Christus Patrem oravit. Joh. 17.
units.tr: The certainty and efficacy of this, so great and so indubitable in its flow toward us, is established by the very close relation of Christ to us, as our surety, priest and king, and of ours to him. He is our head, and we are his members; he is the prince of our salvation, the firstborn brother; he is the vine, we the branches; he is a partaker of our flesh and blood, to the end that he might destroy him who had the power of death and free us from the fear of death. Hence whatever Christ, as such, has done, suffered, acquired and possesses is reckoned as ours, who are his members, his people and his own possession, and is held and confirmed to us as inalienable, since the Father has given it to him as an inheritance. For all these things, and for these alone, Christ prayed to the Father. John 17.

units.la: XXIX.
units.tr: XXIX.

units.la: Consequens hinc est: intentionem Patris & Filii non fuisse, pretium satisfactionis & meriti, ad omnes & singulos sine exceptione extendi, sed in eos omnes, & tantùm, quos Pater dedit ex æterno suo decreto Filio redimendos Joh. 6:39. pro quibus laborem suum Christus impendit. Joh. 17:9. 11. &c. & Pater eos gratia sua cumulavit, in Christo acceptavit. Psal. 16:1.2.5.&c. 2.Cor. 5:19. Et esse tam efficax, ita plenarium & sufficientissimum; ut perfectissimè peccata fidelium omnium, ad Deum per Christum accedentium, omnis ætatis, temporis & loci, ab initio ad finem mundi existentium & exstiturorum abstulerit. Hebr. 7:27. 10:11. 14. 7:25. 1. Joh. 2: 2. Joh. 1:29. Nec iterari, nec quæri alibi, quàm in Christo, debet vel potest. Act. 4:12. Heb. 9:26.27.28. Gal. 4:4. 5:6. Christus enim semel passus, mortuus & resuscitatus, judicatus, justificatus spiritu, & consummatus est in secula. Ergo & qui sunt ipsius. Gloria enim capitis, & quæ lex est spiritus vitæ in ipso, est & membrorum ejus. Habet ergo fides nostra firmum fundamentum. Et ædificium ei inextructum sustinetur immotum.
units.tr: It follows from this that the intention of the Father and the Son was not that the price of satisfaction and merit should extend without exception to all and each, but to all those, and only those, whom the Father from his eternal decree gave to the Son to be redeemed. John 6:39. For these Christ expended his labour. John 17:9, 11, etc. For these the Father has loaded with his grace and accepted in Christ. Ps. 16:1, 2, 5, etc.; 2 Cor. 5:19. And the satisfaction is so efficacious, so full and most sufficient, that it has perfectly taken away the sins of all believers who approach God through Christ, of every age, time and place, who exist or will exist from the beginning to the end of the world. Heb. 7:27; 10:11, 14; 7:25; 1 John 2:2; John 1:29. Nor ought it or can it be repeated, or sought anywhere but in Christ. Acts 4:12; Heb. 9:26, 27, 28; Gal. 4:4; 5:6. For Christ, having suffered once, died and been raised, judged and justified by the Spirit, has been consummated for ever. Therefore so too are those who are his. For the glory of the head, and what is the law of the spirit of life in him, is also of his members. Therefore our faith has a firm foundation, and the building yet to be raised upon it is upheld immovable.

units.la: XXX.
units.tr: XXX.

units.la: Hinc & meritum omne excluditur hominum; sive fingatur esse illud ex pacto, condigno, vel congruo. Solus enim sanguis Christi nos purgat; & qui inutiles servi Dei sumus, vel ipsum motum, ut & alia omnia, ex Deo habentes, quæ ipsi accepta referre, cui nihil commodare possumus, debemus. Externa non respicit Deus, ut homines; in Christo dat nobis regnum, cui emendo impar est bonum & officium omne hominis, ut & omnis creaturæ meræ. Et meritum tale cudere, est sacrilegium committere.
units.tr: Hence all merit of men is also excluded, whether it is imagined to be by covenant, condign, or congruous. For the blood of Christ alone cleanses us, and we, being unprofitable servants of God, ought to ascribe to him, from whom we have them, even the very motion of our will and all other things, since we can lend him nothing to whom we owe them. God does not regard external things as men do; in Christ he gives us the kingdom, for the purchase of which every good work and office of man is unequal, just as every mere creature is. And to coin such a merit is to commit sacrilege.

units.la: XXXI.
units.tr: XXXI.

units.la: Satisfactio jam præstita filiis omnibus Dei libertatem ab elementis mundi, chirographo, servitute, & metu affert. Col. 2:14.15. & sequentibus. Plures efficit filios sterilis, quàm maritatæ, ut latifundia ex gentibus ad Deum & politiam Israëlis adductis pro hereditate possideat. Esa. 54:1.2.3.4.5.6. & sq. Gal. 4:27. Eph. 2:13–22. Et, velo ablato, ut cognitio major; ita affectus filialis erga Deum, ut Patrem; & liberior ad eum accessus, spiritu sancto efficacissimè operante in nobis. Ier. 31:34: Es. 54:13. Hebr. 8:10.11.12. 4:16. 10:22.23. Ut in spiritu & veritate Deum colamus Joh. 4:24. Et Salvatorem, qui sine peccato apparitypus est Hebr. 9:28. interea ædificationi proximi, & regno Dei propagando serio incumbentes, exspectemus.
units.tr: The satisfaction now rendered brings to all the sons of God freedom from the elements of the world, from the handwriting, from servitude and from fear. Col. 2:14, 15 and following. It makes the children of the barren woman more numerous than those of the married wife, so that she may possess as an inheritance the wide lands drawn from the Gentiles to God and to the commonwealth of Israel. Isa. 54:1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and following; Gal. 4:27; Eph. 2:13–22. And, the veil being taken away, our knowledge is greater, and our filial affection toward God as Father is likewise greater, and our access to him is freer, the Holy Spirit working most effectually in us. Jer. 31:34; Isa. 54:13; Heb. 8:10, 11, 12; 4:16; 10:22, 23. So that we may worship God in spirit and truth, John 4:24, and may wait for the Saviour, who will appear without sin, as the type, Heb. 9:28, meanwhile zealously devoting ourselves to the edification of our neighbour and the propagation of the kingdom of God.

units.la: COROLLARIA.
units.tr: COROLLARIES.

units.la: I. Imago Dei, ad quam homo creatus fuit, fuit sapientia in intellectu, & rectitudo in voluntate.
units.tr: I. The image of God, in which man was created, was wisdom in the intellect and rectitude in the will.

units.la: 2. Hoc ipso fuit constitutus sub fœdere operum.
units.tr: 2. By this very fact man was placed under a covenant of works.

units.la: 3. Rectitudo homini data fuit cum mutabilitate.
units.tr: 3. Rectitude was given to man together with mutability.

units.la: 4. Per peccatum primum non Adam tantum reus est factus & corruptus; sed tota ejus posteritas naturaliter ab ipso descendens.
units.tr: 4. Through the first sin, not only Adam was made guilty and corrupted, but also his whole posterity, descending naturally from him.

units.la: 5. Restitui homo ex illo lapsu per redemtionem factam ab eo, qui est Deus simul & homo, potuit, non vero ex viribus propriis.
units.tr: 5. Man could be restored from that fall through the redemption made by him who is God and man at once, but not by his own powers.

units.la: 6. Restitutio illa fit ex mera Dei gratia.
units.tr: 6. That restoration comes from the mere grace of God.

units.la: 7. Gratia semel data est inalienabilis.
units.tr: 7. Grace, once given, is inalienable.

units.la: 8. Christus non condidit leges novas, nec novum pactum.
units.tr: 8. Christ did not enact new laws, nor a new covenant.

units.la: 9. Fideles certi sunt de sua salute.
units.tr: 9. Believers are certain of their salvation.

units.la: 10. Sacramenta N.T. sunt tantum duo. Et non sunt proprie ipsum Testamentum, ut nec ullum Sacramentum.
units.tr: 10. The sacraments of the New Testament are only two. And they are not properly the Testament itself, any more than any sacrament is.

units.la: 11. Sacramenta non tantum sunt signa indicantia rem promissam, sed & confirmantia credentibus.
units.tr: 11. Sacraments are not only signs indicating the promised thing, but also confirm it to believers.

units.la: 12. Baptismus non est jugum, nec tessera Christianitatis ad tempus tan-tum duratura.
units.tr: 12. Baptism is not a yoke, nor a token of Christianity to last only for a time.

units.la: 13. Omnibus fidelium liberis administrandus, & non est iterandus.
units.tr: 13. It is to be administered to all the children of believers, and is not to be repeated.

units.la: 14. Baptismus Johannis Baptista non est diversus à baptismate Christi per Apostolos tradito.
units.tr: 14. The baptism of John the Baptist is not different from the baptism of Christ delivered through the Apostles.

units.la: 15. Sacra cœna non est ipsum sacrificium.
units.tr: 15. The Lord's Supper is not itself a sacrifice.

units.la: 16. Sub utraque specie scil. panis & vini administranda.
units.tr: 16. It is to be administered under both kinds, namely bread and wine.

units.la: 17. Non est Cathedra infallibilis in terra, nec vicarius Christi.
units.tr: 17. There is no infallible chair on earth, nor a vicar of Christ.

units.la: 18. Regimen Ecclesiæ non est Monarchicum quoad homines.
units.tr: 18. The government of the Church is not monarchical with respect to men.

units.la: 19. Religio est propaganda demonstratione veritatis ad conscientiam, non armis.
units.tr: 19. Religion is to be propagated by demonstrating the truth to the conscience, not by arms.

units.la: 20. Conscientia solus Deus dominatur.
units.tr: 20. God alone rules the conscience.

units.la: 21. Obedientia Christi, fidelibus imputata, non tollit, sed ponit sanctificationis necessitatem.
units.tr: 21. The obedience of Christ, imputed to believers, does not abolish but establishes the necessity of sanctification.

units.la: 22. Sanctitas fidelium, sine qua Deum videre non possunt, legem Decalogi mensuram habet.
units.tr: 22. The holiness of believers, without which they cannot see God, has the Decalogue as its measure.

units.la: 23. Et tamen sunt sub gratia, non sub lege.
units.tr: 23. And yet they are under grace, not under law.

units.la: 24. Lex hominem peccatorem non convertit, nec regenerat, vel vivificat.
units.tr: 24. The law does not convert, regenerate, or quicken a sinful man.

units.la: 25. Quicunque est extra Christum, est sub lege.
units.tr: 25. Whoever is outside Christ is under the law.

units.la: 26. Licet ante Christi adventum in carnem omnes Israelita fuerint sub lege; non tamen sine magno discrimine.
units.tr: 26. Although before Christ's coming in the flesh all Israelites were under the law, it was not without great danger.

units.la: 27. Absente Spiritu Sanctificationis, sunt in intellectu tenebræ, in voluntate malitia.
units.tr: 27. Where the Spirit of sanctification is absent, there is darkness in the intellect and malice in the will.

units.la: 28. In sanctificatis, donec aura hujus lucis fruuntur, est pugna inter spiritum & carnem.
units.tr: 28. In the sanctified, as long as they enjoy the breath of this light, there is a struggle between spirit and flesh.

units.la: 29. In irregenitis pugna talis non est, sed affectuum.
units.tr: 29. In the unregenerate there is no such struggle, but only a struggle of the affections.

units.la: 30. Non est medium inter Regenitum, & irregenitum.
units.tr: 30. There is no middle state between the regenerate and the unregenerate.

units.la: 31. Spiritus sanctificans in irreginitis non est.
units.tr: 31. The sanctifying Spirit is not in the unregenerate.

units.la: 32. Apud semel sanctificatos manet semper.
units.tr: 32. With those once sanctified he remains always.

units.la: 33. Regenerati non sunt ita perfecti in hac vita, quin habeant aliquam adhuc vitiositatem sibi adjacentem, qua peccatum est.
units.tr: 33. The regenerate are not so perfect in this life that they do not still have some vice clinging to them, which is sin.

units.la: 34. Sunt tamen veræ pii & accepti Deo.
units.tr: 34. Nevertheless they are truly godly and acceptable to God.

units.la: 35. Si esset possibile, semel regeneratum recidere & à Deo totaliter deficere, esset impossibile eum iterum restaurari.
units.tr: 35. If it were possible for one once regenerated to fall back and wholly fail from God, it would be impossible for him to be restored again.

units.la: 36. Lapsus frequens fidelium ipsis non adimit spem confugiendi ad Christum, nec est interruptio perseverantia.
units.tr: 36. The frequent lapse of believers does not take from them the hope of fleeing to Christ, nor is it an interruption of perseverance.

units.la: 37. Obedientia imperfecta non est justitia coram Deo, nec esse potest.
units.tr: 37. Imperfect obedience is not righteousness before God, nor can it be.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: END.

units.tr: 37. Imperfect obedience is not righteousness before God, nor can it be.
